How many hours did you lose this week to reports, emails, minutes, spreadsheets and paperwork?

Whether you maintain medical equipment, draft contracts, run a business, advise clients or manage projects, a big share of your week goes to repetitive work. AI can take much of it off your desk, if you know how to use it well.

The Centre for Design Innovation & Engineering (CDIE) at Kenyatta University invites you to a FREE teaser session:

🧠 AI AS YOUR SECOND BRAIN – Learn how to Automate the Mundane
📅 Tuesday, 27th October 2026
🕔 5:00 – 7:00 PM (EAT)
💻 100% online – join from anywhere

You will see practical, everyday ways to use AI to:
✅ Draft, summarise and review documents in minutes
✅ Organise notes, research and ideas into a searchable "second brain"
✅ Turn routine tasks into repeatable workflows
✅ Use AI responsibly, with judgement, accuracy and confidentiality in mind

No coding or technical background needed. This session is a preview of our 4-week AI Strategy Masterclass (virtual, November, Tue & Thu, 6–8 PM).

👉 Reserve your free spot: https://lnkd.in/dxnmwge4 
📞 0759 158430 | ✉️ ive@ku.ac.ke | 🌐 cdie.co.ke

Know a colleague drowning in admin? Invite them to attend.

🤖 AI MASTERCLASS — NOVEMBER INTAKE 🤖

AI is rewriting the rules of work. In this 4-week virtual masterclass, we'll teach you how to use AI as Your Second Brain 🧠. 

Offload the mental clutter. Organize your thinking, capture insights, and make faster decisions with AI-powered workflows.

Program Cost: Ksh. 20,000

To help you decide, we are offering a free module on how to use AI to Automate the Mundane. This session will help you reclaim 5-10 hours a week by automating email drafting, meeting summaries, research and reporting. 

Sign up for the free teaser session here: https://lnkd.in/dxnmwge4

To register for the masterclass, follow the link: https://lnkd.in/dcHYrJvi

Kenyatta University Rice University The Lemelson Foundation MedTech Kenyatta University Stacy Awinja , MIEEE Eubrea Mitchy Anthonius Waka

Great ideas start with spotting the right problem.

Yesterday, our MSc Biomedical Engineering (MDI) Cohort 2 engaged with Eng. Millicent Alooh, HSC,    PhD Candidate for an intensive BME 816 design session, learning how to move from a raw pain point on the hospital floor to a viable medical product.

From understanding the realities of healthcare delivery, such as unpacking why nearly 95% of Kenya's medical devices are imported to framing user-centered need statements, our engineers are learning to build solutions that truly matter.
